title: Eventual properness over qcqs scheme limits
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed: the diagonal is a closed immersion, the map is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts, and every algebraic-space base change is closed on underlying point spaces. Let $J$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_j)_{j\in J}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, and $T=\varprojlim_j T_j$. Fix $j_0\in J$ and a finitely presented algebraic space $Z_{j_0}\to T_{j_0}$. For $j\ge j_0$ put $Z_j=Z_{j_0}\times_{T_{j_0}}T_j$ and put $Z=Z_{j_0}\times_{T_{j_0}}T$. If $Z\to T$ is proper, then $Z_j\to T_j$ is proper for some $j\ge j_0$, and for every later stage. The bases $T_j$ need not be affine.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $T_{j_0}=\bigcup_{a\in A}U_{a,0}$ by [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open], applied to the whole quasi-compact scheme. For $j\ge j_0$ put $U_{a,j}=T_j\times_{T_{j_0}}U_{a,0}$ and put $U_a=T\times_{T_{j_0}}U_{a,0}$. These are open subschemes by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; their underlying opens are the inverse images of $U_{a,0}$, since factoring a map through that open means its image lies there. Thus they cover $T_j$ and $T$, respectively. Each $U_{a,j}\to U_{a,0}$ is affine by base change of the affine transition $T_j\to T_{j_0}$, hence $U_{a,j}$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the restricted transitions are affine and $U_a=\varprojlim_{j\ge j_0}U_{a,j}$ with these projections. The upper tail is a small nonempty directed set with least element $j_0$.

For each $a$ set $W_{a,0}=Z_{j_0}\times_{T_{j_0}}U_{a,0}$. Its map to $U_{a,0}$ is finitely presented, and the map $W_a=Z\times_TU_a\to U_a$ is proper, by the separate finite-presentation and proper base-change clauses of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The sheaf fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies
$$W_{a,0}\times_{U_{a,0}}U_{a,j}\cong Z_j\times_{T_j}U_{a,j},\qquad W_{a,0}\times_{U_{a,0}}U_a\cong W_a.$$
Indeed on a test scheme both sides specify a section of $Z_{j_0}$ and a section of $U_{a,j}$ (respectively $U_a$) with equal images in $T_{j_0}$; forgetting or restoring the redundant intermediate coordinates gives inverse natural maps over the indicated base.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-eventually-proper] separately to the inverse system of affine schemes $(U_{a,j})_{j\ge j_0}$ and its finitely presented space $W_{a,0}$. Step 1 gives its limit and affine transitions, and step 2 gives its proper limiting morphism. Obtain $i_a\ge j_0$ such that $Z_j\times_{T_j}U_{a,j}\to U_{a,j}$ is proper for every $j\ge i_a$. Directedness supplies a common upper bound $i$ for $j_0$ and the finitely many $i_a$: start with $j_0$ and successively take binary upper bounds. When $A$ is empty take $i=j_0$. For every $j\ge i$, all the restrictions to the covering opens $U_{a,j}$ are therefore proper.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), apply the affine-base case on a finite affine covering and take a common stage.

proof.text: Fix $j\ge i$. The open covering $\{U_{a,j}\to T_j\}_{a\in A}$ is an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. To check the hypotheses explicitly, an open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. At each source point choose an affine neighbourhood contained in that open on the target and use the same neighbourhood on the source. The induced ring map is $R\to R$, so local finite presentation follows with zero generators and zero relations from [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; the stalk map is an isomorphism, so its target is a free rank-one module and is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Joint surjectivity is exactly the covering equality of step 1. Apply the properness locality clause of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] to $Z_j\to T_j$ and this fppf covering: every pullback is proper by step 3, hence $Z_j\to T_j$ is proper. This works for every $j\ge i$, including $i$ itself. The empty cover of an empty base is allowed: joint surjectivity is vacuous there, and there are no local conditions to check.
